questions.q: In the example this course follows, who is the seller (the Oracle Fusion customer running O2C) and who is the buyer?
options: Both companies are the same entity
Harborview Industrial Supply is the seller; LTV Manufacturing Corporation is the buyer
LTV Manufacturing Corporation is the seller; Harborview Industrial Supply is the buyer
Neither company places or receives the order
questions.explain: LTV Manufacturing Corporation sells to its customer, Harborview Industrial Supply, on order SO-48217.

questions.q: What is the net order total for SO-48217 after the volume discount?
questions.explain: $58,000.00 list total minus a 5% ($2,900.00) volume discount equals $55,100.00 net.

questions.q: What are the payment terms on SO-48217?
questions.explain: SO-48217 is agreed with Net 30 terms.

questions.q: Is LTV Manufacturing Corporation a real company referenced from public records?
options: Yes, it is a real Fortune 500 manufacturer
No — it is explicitly a fictional company created for this course's examples
Yes, it is Harborview's parent company
It is an actual Oracle customer named in Oracle's documentation
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that LTV Manufacturing Corporation and Harborview Industrial Supply are fictional, created for this course.

questions.q: According to the roadmap, what happens to SO-48217 in Chapter 3?
options: It is paid off in full
It is posted to the General Ledger
It is picked, packed, and shipped, alongside a look at a separate damaged-goods return
questions.explain: Chapter 3 (Fulfillment and Shipping) covers the warehouse picking, packing, and shipping the order, plus a returns scenario.
